proposed_from.topic: Exact fixed-bin recovery of acyclic Hawkes graphs from two covariance lags. For a stationary labeled multivariate linear Hawkes process with known bin width Delta, positive baselines, a common unknown exponential decay, nonnegative zero-diagonal acyclic excitation matrix, and at least one edge, prove that the mean plus Gamma_1 and Gamma_2 identify beta, every edge amplitude, and the baselines. Establish Gamma_k=exp((A-beta I)(k-1)Delta)J^2K, im Gamma_1=im A, recovery of beta from the restricted transition, exact finite nilpotent-log deconvolution, and edge recovery from the antisymmetric covariance jump. Cover singular A, repeated poles, disconnected components, and zero-edge nonidentification; derive rank-adaptive consistent estimation, support recovery, and simultaneous graph confidence sets. Consumer: Qiao et al.'s metropolitan cellular-alarm logs recorded at 1–9 second resolution. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived K=A(2 beta I-A)Q with Q positive definite and A_ij=max(K_ij-K_ji,0)/lambda_j; a covariance-only Gamma_0,Gamma_1,Gamma_2 corollary also emerged. Recovery passed 400 random/adversarial DAGs (p=2–9, worst error 8.31e-10), 24 independent bin-integral checks, and 207 three-node alias searches. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete a basis-invariant HAC/rank-truncation delta-method proof with explicit conditioning margins and independently audit the two-lag algebra. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce diamond and proportional-row cases by independent quadrature; any legal violation of im Gamma_1=im A or the recovered covariance limit kills the theorem. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest fixed-bin second-order method, Koyama2025, proves a small-bin spectral expansion for a coarse-grained process rather than exact recovery for the original process at arbitrary fixed \(\Delta\). Kirchner2016 is also asymptotic in the mesh, and its lag equations motivate rather than solve finite-lag inversion. The closest population identification results observe strictly richer objects: BacryMuzy2016 uses the complete covariance-density function, EtesamiZhangSinghalKiyavash2016 uses full spectral zeros and covariance-density Laplace transforms, and ZhouPapadogeorgou2025 uses the full aggregated-count distribution. The central theorem instead gives a closed-form, basis-invariant inverse from one mean vector and two fixed-bin covariance matrices under a contribution-defining labeled feed-forward acyclicity restriction. The singular case is nonroutine because \(\Gamma_1\) need not be invertible, repeated eigenvalues preclude eigenvector matching, and direction follows only after the skew-jump identity. The covariance-only theorem is an additional field-level result. Fixed-margin inference distinguishes vanishing-threshold support consistency from conservative fixed-level graph inclusion, while one-lag fibers and boundary-honest adaptation remain explicitly unresolved.
seed_list: Exact recovery of a nonempty acyclic common-decay Hawkes graph from the stationary mean and exactly two positive fixed-bin covariance lags.
A necessary-and-sufficient information-order frontier showing when one positive covariance lag fails and two lags suffice.
Covariance-only recovery from the zero lag and two positive lags, with no separately supplied mean.
A finite-lag matrix-pencil frontier for acyclic Hawkes networks with edge-specific exponential decay rates.
An exact observational-equivalence characterization for cyclic common-decay Hawkes networks observed through two covariance lags.
Basis-invariant rank-adaptive limit theory for the nonlinear two-lag inverse on fixed conditioning-margin strata.
Honest graph confidence sets across unknown rank, local-to-zero edges, and the empty-graph stratum.
A calibrated overidentification test based on surplus covariance lags against heterogeneous decay, cycles, and nonexponential kernels.

seed_details.one_line: Recover \((\beta,A,\mu)\) by restricting the observable semigroup to \(\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)\), taking a finite nilpotent logarithm, and orienting edges through the antisymmetric covariance jump.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Mean plus two positive-lag covariance matrices for every nonzero acyclic common-decay model.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the full-frequency zero and pole extraction of Etesami et al. and the full Wiener--Hopf equation of Bacry and Muzy by a basis-invariant restriction of \(\Gamma_2\Gamma_1^{+}\) to \(\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for fixed-bin Hawkes covariance lags, matrix logarithms, and finite-lag graph recovery returned full-spectrum, likelihood, aggregated-distribution, and vanishing-bin methods, but no exact two-lag inverse.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from BacryMuzy2016 because second-order statistics already identify the Hawkes kernel.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem observes the entire covariance-density function and solves an infinite-dimensional Wiener--Hopf equation; it neither proves that two bin integrals suffice nor handles the singular image restriction created by acyclic \(A\).

seed_details.one_line: Characterize the one-lag compatibility fiber and prove an information-order frontier: two positive lags identify every nonempty model, while one lag fails on a nondegenerate region.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Exact two-lag recovery and its minimality.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After constructing the two-lag inverse, replace sufficiency algebra by elimination of \((\beta,A,\mu)\) from the one-lag moment fiber and a positivity-preserving reverse witness.
seed_details.destination_search: Targeted searches found no necessary-lag theorem for fixed-bin Hawkes covariance moments; the nearest finite-information result uses the full law of at least three aggregated bins.
seed_details.referee_objection: Dimension counting makes one-lag failure automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The observable covariance matrix has more scalar entries than the parameter vector, so dimension counting does not settle failure; a legal positive-baseline fiber or a generic injectivity proof is required.

seed_details.one_line: Recover the innovation-intensity diagonal from the zero-bin covariance jump and thereby identify the entire model from \((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\) alone.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Covariance-only recovery without a separately supplied stationary mean.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Separate the diagonal innovation contribution in \(\Gamma_0\) after reconstructing the positive-lag covariance density, instead of treating first-order intensity as an external input.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for covariance-only finite-bin Hawkes identification found full Bartlett spectra and second-plus-third cumulant matching, but no three-covariance formula.
seed_details.referee_objection: The diagonal of \(\Gamma_0\) plainly equals the mean count.
seed_details.rebuttal: Within-bin descendants add a non-diagonal and diagonal excitation covariance term, so the Poisson jump must be subtracted using the reconstructed continuous positive-lag covariance.

seed_details.one_line: Determine the minimal covariance-lag Hankel order for edge-specific exponential decay by a matrix-pencil realization theorem with collision counterexamples.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Finite-lag identification under heterogeneous edge decays.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the logarithm of one restricted transition by minimal realization of a matrix-valued exponential sum.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining heterogeneous Hawkes decay with matrix pencils and Prony recovery found latent-time likelihood and general system-identification methods, but no legal finite-bin Hawkes minimality theorem.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is ordinary Prony recovery applied entrywise.
seed_details.rebuttal: Shared latent paths couple poles across entries, repeated edge decays collide, and causal amplitudes must satisfy Hawkes positivity and acyclic path constraints; entrywise Prony does not certify a common legal network realization.

seed_details.one_line: Describe exactly which cyclic common-decay Hawkes parameterizations share the same mean and first two bin-covariance lags.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: The boundary of acyclic two-lag identification.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace nilpotent logarithm uniqueness and antisymmetric one-direction orientation by a compatibility-fiber analysis over stable cyclic matrices.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found full-spectrum identification for cyclic exponential Hawkes systems, but no two-bin-lag equivalence class.
seed_details.referee_objection: Two lags obviously cannot identify a general cyclic matrix.
seed_details.rebuttal: Nonidentification alone is not the proposed result; the contribution would be the exact labeled fiber and the necessary-and-sufficient restriction restoring injectivity.

seed_details.one_line: Derive a basis-invariant delta method for the rank-truncated two-lag inverse and a joint limit law for decay, amplitudes, and baselines.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Rank-adaptive estimation and graph-wide inference from empirical \(\Gamma_1\) and \(\Gamma_2\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the smooth Whittle score expansion by a spectral-projector expansion of an estimated nonsymmetric covariance image followed by differentiation of a restricted matrix logarithm.
seed_details.destination_search: The fixed-bin limit literature does not combine random-rank image estimation with Hawkes graph inversion; exact-time confidence procedures use martingale likelihood scores instead.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a routine delta method after identification.
seed_details.rebuttal: The inverse is not ambiently smooth when \(A\) is singular, and a proof must be invariant to the random image basis and control the rank threshold, restricted logarithm, and dependent-data long-run covariance jointly.

seed_details.one_line: Construct one graph confidence set that remains honest when rank, topological order, edge strength, and even identification of \(\beta\) change discontinuously.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Honest inference across weak-rank and empty-network strata.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace fixed-margin delta-method intervals by inversion of local experiments and confidence unions across candidate image ranks.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found exact-time Hawkes confidence polyhedra and fixed-model binned asymptotics, but no confidence set valid at the empty-graph nonidentification boundary.
seed_details.referee_objection: Returning every graph near zero is trivially honest.
seed_details.rebuttal: The target includes a matching lower bound on expected inclusion loss or diameter and an attaining adaptive procedure away from the boundary.

seed_details.one_line: Use \(\Gamma_3,\ldots,\Gamma_L\) as overidentifying semigroup restrictions and calibrate a specification test under dependent bin counts.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Surplus-lag diagnostics for common decay and acyclicity.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace cumulant-matching estimation by a projected covariance residual whose nuisance parameters are obtained from the first two lags.
seed_details.destination_search: No located paper tests the fixed-bin restricted-semigroup identity against heterogeneous decay, feedback, and nonexponential alternatives.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is an ordinary generalized-method-of-moments overidentification test.
seed_details.rebuttal: The residual is rank constrained and plugs in a nonsmooth image-and-logarithm inverse, so ordinary chi-square calibration fails near rank changes and weak edges.

proposed_from.literature_map: Bacry and Muzy (2016) identify a stationary Hawkes kernel from the entire first-order intensity and continuous covariance-density function through a Wiener--Hopf equation. Etesami et al. (2016) recover exponential Hawkes graphs by locating modes in the full covariance spectrum and transforming a covariance-density estimate. Zhou and Papadogeorgou (2025) identify parametric Hawkes specifications from the full distribution of aggregated counts by comparing probabilities of sparse bin configurations; their exponential result requires at least three aggregated bins but does not reduce the observable law to two covariance matrices. Shlomovich, Cohen, and Adams (2022) estimate multivariate binned Hawkes models with edge-specific decays by latent-time Monte Carlo expectation maximization and state no finite-moment injectivity theorem. Qiao et al. (2023) show why coarse timestamps destroy ordinary within-bin Granger ordering and motivate a structural solution for cellular-alarm data. Cheysson and Lang (2022) supply mixing-based Whittle asymptotics for fixed-bin counts, while Boly, Cheysson, and Nguyen (2024) give multivariate Hawkes mixing and functional central limit results; neither differentiates a random image projection or restricted matrix logarithm. Achab et al. (2017) add third-order integrated cumulants to estimate the integrated kernel, rather than extracting intensity from zero-lag covariance. Wang et al. (2020) and Wang, Kolar, and Shojaie (2025) quantify network uncertainty from exact event times, not from fixed-bin covariance inversion. Jin and Huang (2026) use a vanishing-bin autoregressive approximation and covariance-rank faithfulness for latent causal discovery, so their limit experiment does not subsume exact fixed-width de-aliasing. Across these adjacent threads, the exact target--method pair---fixed \(\Delta\), labeled acyclic common-decay Hawkes law, stationary mean, and only \(\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\), inverted on \(\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)\)---is unoccupied.

banked_reason: Operator stop: sound point-process identifiability, but no causal anchor. Zero occurrences of do/intervention/confounding/causal-sufficiency/potential-outcome in the core; none of its 20 assumptions is causal; all 19 references are point-process, time-series or matrix-analysis. Recovering G(A) is Granger-style structure identification whose causal reading needs a causal-sufficiency assumption the paper never states and a literature it never cites.
